## Findings

**1–2. Governing policy.** Cigna carves out musculoskeletal surgical prior authorization (including shoulder arthroplasty, CPT 23472) to **EviCore healthcare**. The document containing the medical‑necessity criteria Cigna applies to CPT 23472 is:

- **Title:** *Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines — CMM‑318: Shoulder Arthroplasty/Replacement/Resurfacing/Revision/Arthrodesis*
- **Policy number:** CMM‑318
- **Current version applicable at the time of this denial (notice dated 2026‑08‑04):** Version 2.0.2025, **Effective March 7, 2026**, published 11/24/2025
- **URL:** https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-11/Cigna_CMM-318_Shoulder%20Arthro%20Replace%20Revision_V2.0.2025_Eff03.07.2026_pub11.24.2025.pdf
- A prior version (V1.0.2024, effective 8/1/2024, later minor-updated 7/1/2025) is at: https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-05/Cigna_CMM-318_Shoul_Arthro_Final_V1.0.2024_eff08.01.2024_update_pub03.07.2025_upd05.29.2025.pdf

**Important caveat on the criteria text:** The current (V2.0.2025) PDF is a 37‑page document, and my automated retrieval of it was cut off after the "Definitions" and "General Guidelines" sections — before reaching the specific "Total Shoulder Arthroplasty (Replacement) Indications" section (page 12). I could not confirm the verbatim current wording of that section. I was able to fully retrieve that section from the **immediately preceding version (V1.0.2024)**, which was in force through early 2026 and whose "Total Shoulder Arthroplasty" indications Cigna's own July‑2025 update memo described as receiving only "minor clinical changes." I'm quoting that version below as the best-evidenced text, but the patient/provider should pull the live current PDF (link above) and check pp. 12–14 to confirm the exact current wording before finalizing the appeal, since it may not be identical.

**3. Medical-necessity criteria (as retrieved, V1.0.2024 text — verify against current V2.0.2025 pp.12-14):**

> "Total shoulder arthroplasty (replacement) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:
> - Radiographic imaging and/or an advanced diagnostic procedure (i.e., MRI, CT) is conclusive for the presence of advanced destructive degenerative joint disease (i.e., osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis) with marked narrowing of the joint space that correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings including ANY of the following:
>   - Irregular joint surfaces
>   - Glenoid sclerosis
>   - Glenoid osteophyte changes
>   - Flattened glenoid
>   - Cystic changes in the humeral head
> - Symptoms include function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment) for at least three (3) months
> - Failure of at least three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management"

The document was truncated before the "Total Shoulder Arthroplasty (Replacement) Non‑Indications" list, so I did not capture the full disqualifying-conditions list; the parallel Hemi‑Arthroplasty Non‑Indications list (which likely shares similar exclusions such as active infection, uncontrolled comorbidities, Charcot joint, etc.) was retrieved but is not confirmed to apply identically to total shoulder arthroplasty.

**4. Appeal deadline:** Per the denial notice itself, the internal appeal must be **received within 180 days of the notice date (2026‑08‑04), i.e., by 2027‑01‑31**. (Note: Cigna's Colorado-specific customer appeal form separately references a 365‑day window for a "Level 1" internal appeal and 180 days for a "Level 2" appeal — but the deadline stated on your actual denial letter, 180 days/by 2027‑01‑31, controls for this claim; if there is any ambiguity, call Cigna member services to confirm which timeline applies to your specific plan.)

**5. Where/how to submit the appeal:**
- This is a **pre-service precertification denial**, which Cigna processes as a **Customer (member) Appeal**. It can be submitted by the patient or by the provider on the patient's behalf.
- **Mail:** Cigna Healthcare National Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188011, Chattanooga, TN 37422 (this is the address on Cigna's own Colorado customer appeal form and matches Cigna's general "all other appeals" address).
- Because the medical-necessity review was performed by **EviCore** on Cigna's behalf, some EviCore-related appeals route to a separate address (EviCore Claim Appeals, P.O. Box 5620, Hartford, CT 06102) — the specific fax number and/or portal to use should be on the actual denial letter or confirmed by calling the member-services number on the back of the Cigna ID card (Cigna general number: 1‑800‑882‑4462; National Appeals Unit: 704‑752‑5241).
- **Recommended practice:** Use the "Cigna HealthCare of Colorado, Inc. Customer Appeal Request" form (https://www.cigna.com/static/www-cigna-com/docs/co-appeal-form.pdf), mark it "Medical Necessity," attach the denial letter, operative/clinic notes, imaging reports, and a letter from the surgeon addressing each bullet of the CMM‑318 Total Shoulder Arthroplasty indications above (radiographic findings, duration/severity of function‑limiting pain, and documentation of ≥3 months of failed non‑surgical management).

## Findings

**1–2. Governing policy.** Cigna carves out musculoskeletal surgical prior authorization (including shoulder arthroplasty, CPT 23472) to **EviCore healthcare**. The document containing the medical‑necessity criteria Cigna applies to CPT 23472 is:

- **Title:** *Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines — CMM‑318: Shoulder Arthroplasty/Replacement/Resurfacing/Revision/Arthrodesis*
- **Policy number:** CMM‑318
- **Current version applicable at the time of this denial (notice dated 2026‑08‑04):** Version 2.0.2025, **Effective March 7, 2026**, published 11/24/2025
- **URL:** https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-11/Cigna_CMM-318_Shoulder%20Arthro%20Replace%20Revision_V2.0.2025_Eff03.07.2026_pub11.24.2025.pdf
- A prior version (V1.0.2024, effective 8/1/2024, later minor-updated 7/1/2025) is at: https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-05/Cigna_CMM-318_Shoul_Arthro_Final_V1.0.2024_eff08.01.2024_update_pub03.07.2025_upd05.29.2025.pdf

**Important caveat on the criteria text:** The current (V2.0.2025) PDF is a 37‑page document, and my automated retrieval of it was cut off after the "Definitions" and "General Guidelines" sections — before reaching the specific "Total Shoulder Arthroplasty (Replacement) Indications" section (page 12). I could not confirm the verbatim current wording of that section. I was able to fully retrieve that section from the **immediately preceding version (V1.0.2024)**, which was in force through early 2026 and whose "Total Shoulder Arthroplasty" indications Cigna's own July‑2025 update memo described as receiving only "minor clinical changes." I'm quoting that version below as the best-evidenced text, but the patient/provider should pull the live current PDF (link above) and check pp. 12–14 to confirm the exact current wording before finalizing the appeal, since it may not be identical.

**3. Medical-necessity criteria (as retrieved, V1.0.2024 text — verify against current V2.0.2025 pp.12-14):**

> "Total shoulder arthroplasty (replacement) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:
> - Radiographic imaging and/or an advanced diagnostic procedure (i.e., MRI, CT) is conclusive for the presence of advanced destructive degenerative joint disease (i.e., osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis) with marked narrowing of the joint space that correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings including ANY of the following:
>   - Irregular joint surfaces
>   - Glenoid sclerosis
>   - Glenoid osteophyte changes
>   - Flattened glenoid
>   - Cystic changes in the humeral head
> - Symptoms include function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment) for at least three (3) months
> - Failure of at least three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management"

The document was truncated before the "Total Shoulder Arthroplasty (Replacement) Non‑Indications" list, so I did not capture the full disqualifying-conditions list; the parallel Hemi‑Arthroplasty Non‑Indications list (which likely shares similar exclusions such as active infection, uncontrolled comorbidities, Charcot joint, etc.) was retrieved but is not confirmed to apply identically to total shoulder arthroplasty.

**4. Appeal deadline:** Per the denial notice itself, the internal appeal must be **received within 180 days of the notice date (2026‑08‑04), i.e., by 2027‑01‑31**. (Note: Cigna's Colorado-specific customer appeal form separately references a 365‑day window for a "Level 1" internal appeal and 180 days for a "Level 2" appeal — but the deadline stated on your actual denial letter, 180 days/by 2027‑01‑31, controls for this claim; if there is any ambiguity, call Cigna member services to confirm which timeline applies to your specific plan.)

**5. Where/how to submit the appeal:**
- This is a **pre-service precertification denial**, which Cigna processes as a **Customer (member) Appeal**. It can be submitted by the patient or by the provider on the patient's behalf.
- **Mail:** Cigna Healthcare National Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188011, Chattanooga, TN 37422 (this is the address on Cigna's own Colorado customer appeal form and matches Cigna's general "all other appeals" address).
- Because the medical-necessity review was performed by **EviCore** on Cigna's behalf, some EviCore-related appeals route to a separate address (EviCore Claim Appeals, P.O. Box 5620, Hartford, CT 06102) — the specific fax number and/or portal to use should be on the actual denial letter or confirmed by calling the member-services number on the back of the Cigna ID card (Cigna general number: 1‑800‑882‑4462; National Appeals Unit: 704‑752‑5241).
- **Recommended practice:** Use the "Cigna HealthCare of Colorado, Inc. Customer Appeal Request" form (https://www.cigna.com/static/www-cigna-com/docs/co-appeal-form.pdf), mark it "Medical Necessity," attach the denial letter, operative/clinic notes, imaging reports, and a letter from the surgeon addressing each bullet of the CMM‑318 Total Shoulder Arthroplasty indications above (radiographic findings, duration/severity of function‑limiting pain, and documentation of ≥3 months of failed non‑surgical management).
